questions_and_answers.question_text: How does the noun guòqù differ from the verb guòqu?
What does duō express before a state verb?
What does a question word + dōu express?
Which adverb can replace dōu when bù or méi is used?
What is unusual about kànbuqǐ among resultative compounds?
Write the Chinese for "What a beautiful child!"
Write the Chinese for "No place is as good as here."

answers.answer_text: Nǎr dōu méi zhèr hǎo" (or "Nǎr yě méi zhèr hǎo.")

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does the positive form kàndeqǐ mean?

answers.answer_text: "To think a lot of," "to think highly of."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "It doesn't matter who you tell it to."

answers.answer_text: Gēn shéi shuō dōu méi guānxi.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Where is guòqù most commonly placed?

answers.answer_text: At the very beginning of the sentence, before the subject.

articles.text:
5. A: Guòqù, Zhōngguo rén chū guó   In the past how difficult it was for
      niàn shū duō nán!             Chinese to go abroad to study!
   B: Xiànzài hǎo le, zǒu dào nǎr  Now it's better, no matter where they
      yě méi rén kànbuqǐ le.        go, no one looks down on them anymore.

Notes on No. 5

guòqù: "the past." Distinguish this NOUN from the VERB "to pass," which in Běijīng has a neutral-tone qu: guòqu. Since it is a time word, guòqù may go either before the subject or between the subject and verb. Most commonly it is placed at the VERY BEGINNING of the sentence.

Guòqù, tā zài Xiānggǎngde        In the past, when he was in Hong Kong,
shíhou, tā jiāo shū.             he taught school.
Nà dōu shi guòqùde shì le!       Those are all things of the past!

duō nán: "how difficult!" Duō, in Běijīng often pronounced duó, is used BEFORE A STATE VERB to express a HIGH DEGREE, like "how" in English:

Jīntian tiānqì duō hǎo.          How nice the weather is today.
Duō piàoliangde háizi a!         What a beautiful child!
Nǐ kàn tā duō xǐhuan niàn shū.   Look at how he loves to study.

zǒu dào nǎr yě méi rén kànbuqǐ: Nǎr here is used as an INDEFINITE PRONOUN, "anywhere, no matter where." A question word (shéi, shénme, něige, nǎr) followed by dōu before the verb expresses the idea of "ANY." When the verb has bù or méi before it, the pattern expresses "nobody, nothing, neither, nowhere."

Shéi dōu kěyi qù.                Anyone may go.
Shéi dōu bù kěyi qù.             No one may go.
Nǎr dōu kěyi qù.                 You can go anywhere.
Nǎr dōu méi zhèr hǎo.            No place is as good as here.

When bù or méi is used before the verb, the adverb YĚ can be used IN PLACE OF dōu:

Shéi yě bù kěyi qù.              No one can go.
Nǎr yě méi zhèr hǎo.             No place is as good as here.

The "any/no" expression may be the SUBJECT, the OBJECT, or the object of a PREPOSITIONAL VERB:

Mài gěi shéi dōu kěyi.           It's okay to sell it to anyone.
Fàng zài nǎr dōu yíyàng.         It's the same wherever you put it.
Gēn shéi shuō dōu méi guānxi.    It doesn't matter who you tell it to.

kànbuqǐ: A resultative compound verb meaning "to look down on, to scorn, to despise." UNLIKE other resultative verb compounds, this one occurs ONLY with -de- or -bu-.

Wǒ zuì kànbuqǐ zhèiyàngde rén.   I despise this kind of person most.

The positive form kàndeqǐ means "to think a lot of," "to think highly of."
